title: 第1章 欢迎来到美利坚第2章 骑士堂吉诃德
slug: 人在美利坚我的叔叔堂吉诃德
content_zh:
美利坚，纽约，肯尼迪机场。
当李维背着自己的全部家当，来到美利坚投奔自己的远房叔叔堂吉诃德的时候，他原本有些阴郁的内心还有些激动。
李维的父母在生前曾经多次跟他提起这个兄弟。据说他当初的行为很不端正，就是说他曾经挥霍过一些钱财，只不过后面又说自己赚了点钱，还尝试邀请李维一家子到美利坚去聚一聚，只不过都被李维的父亲给拒绝了。
李维从未见过这个叔叔，只是从父亲的嘴里听说过一些他的故事，如今他家庭巨变，17岁的他父母双亡，还欠了一大笔钱，如果留在国内就会因为还不起钱而成为老赖，而李维并不想这么做。
好在按照两国的法律条款，外事部的人为他联系到了自己这位美利坚的远方叔叔。
堂吉诃德，李维一边提着2个行李一边咀嚼着这个名字，好古怪的名字。
突然，他的电话响了起来，这张手机卡还是国内外事部门的一个姐姐给他办的。
“我是堂吉诃德·塞万提斯，”一个沙哑、急促的中年男音说道，背景音里面还有汽车转向灯的哒哒声，“听着，我不进停车场，那里面是吸血鬼开的，停车费要4美金一小时，你现在在哪里？”
得亏李维从小英语耳濡目染，相当于半个母语了，不然他还没办法听清楚这位名叫堂吉诃德·塞万提斯的叔叔的话。
他真的赚到了一些钱吗？李维不禁有些怀疑，不然为什么会因为4美金一小时的停车费而如此焦躁。
“我是李维，”他说道，“我刚刚过海关。”
“那你去T4航站楼，B区，2号门外，还有5分钟到的时候给我打电话，”堂吉诃德的声音十分急促，“别太早打电话，听明白了吗？我不能停太久，该死的交警正在盯着我。”
电话挂断，李维有些呆滞地站在原地，思考要不要用花呗再刷一张机票回去。
10分钟之后，一辆破旧的小车带着侧裙边的泥点子停在了路边的车道，差点撞上了一辆黄色的出租车。
李维花了不少功夫才从厚厚的灰浆和铁锈中认出这是一辆原本为白色的丰田。车窗摇下之后，露出了一张瘦削、颧骨突出、一脸胡茬的脸，他的眼睛上挂着长期缺乏睡眠导致的眼袋。
“上车！”他的眼神滴溜溜地转，仿佛在寻找着不存在的交警，“快点儿，别磨蹭。”
李维有些费力地把两个死沉的箱子摔进满是灰尘和空油漆桶的后车车厢中，掰开副驾驶的门然后钻了进去。
副驾驶的座位上还扔着一件满是油漆点的反光背心和一个半空的佳得乐瓶子，李维有些嫌弃地把它们扔到后座才能坐下。
“呜！”
堂吉诃德一脚油门踩下去，丰田发出一声惨叫，并未像骑士的战马那样冲锋，而是迟缓地颤抖着挤入了车流。

“系好安全带，”他转过来说道，“副驾驶的门锁坏了，拐弯的时候可能会弹开。”
李维不禁抬起一只手抓住了头顶的把手。
“李维，是吧？”堂吉诃德说道，“听着，我对你的父亲......我同父异母的哥哥和嫂子的去世......我很遗憾，他是个真正聪明的家伙，结果因为一场可笑的车祸而去世......听说你还赔了一大笔钱？这是赔不起了跑来美利坚了吗？”
“我会挣到钱然后把欠的钱还上的，而且这不关你的事，”李维皱了皱眉头，“这是我自己的事情，我成年了就会去打工赚钱。”
这就是父亲生前说的“赚了点钱”的叔叔？
“但是他把你扔给我的时候，可没有带一张一百万美金的支票，”堂吉诃德嗤笑了一声，“纽约不比天朝，这里金钱可以买来一切，但是也代表着一切都要用金钱来买，所以，你兜里有多少钱？”
“大概......卡里有600美金，”李维说道，“剩下的就是我的衣服和一些日用品。”
其实他有2张卡，另外一张里面有足足6000美金，只是他没说。
这笔钱拿去还债杯水车薪，但是对于他现在来说无疑是一笔足以在关键时刻救命的巨款。
但是即便是600美金，在这个叔叔面前也显得有些惊喜。
“600块？哈！”他猛拍了一下方向盘，“好吧，至少够付这周的油费和我的误工费了。欢迎来到美利坚！小子。”
在一路的絮絮叨叨之中，李维都不用说，堂吉诃德自然而然地如同竹筒倒豆子一般地讲述出了他的故事。
从他做生意发了一笔小财开始，到认识了他的前妻（“那可真是个纯粹的臭碧池，不是吗？女人就是这样，恨不得榨干你所有的骨髓”），再然后离婚，资金链出了问题周转不开，他去向黑帮借了高利贷的同时还要每个月支付前妻2000美金的赡养费（“该死的美利坚法律，让一头猪躺在家里还要每个月还能赚2000美金，如果我再早个10年，我都恨不得去卖屁股赚钱了。”）。
“所以现在我要打2份工才能够活下去，”他点了一支烟，淡淡做出了总结，“白天在建筑工地里面搬砖，晚上在一家西班牙餐厅的后厨洗盘子，这就是美利坚，想活下去你就得拼尽全力.......到了。”
“这是哪儿？”李维透过满是油污的车窗，打量着窗外像是发霉大面包的灰色混凝土建筑。
这里显然不像是堂吉诃德的家。
content_en:
USA, New York, JFK Airport.
When Li Wei carried all his belongings and came to America to join his distant uncle Don Quixote, he was still a little excited in his originally gloomy heart.
Levi's parents mentioned this brother to him many times during his lifetime. It is said that his behavior was very improper at first, that is to say, he once squandered some money, but later said that he had made some money, and tried to invite Levi's family to the United States for a reunion, but Levi's father rejected them all.
Levi has never met this uncle, but has only heard some stories about him from his father's mouth. Now his family has undergone tremendous changes. Both his parents have died when he was 17 years old, and he still owes a large sum of money. If he stays in the country, he will become an old man because he cannot pay back the money, but Levi does not want to do this.
Fortunately, in accordance with the legal provisions of the two countries, people from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs contacted his distant uncle in the United States for him.
Don Quixote, Levi was chewing on this name while carrying two luggages, what a weird name.
Suddenly, his phone rang. This mobile phone card was issued to him by a sister in the domestic and foreign affairs department.
"I'm Don Quixote Cervantes," said a hoarse, rapid middle-aged male voice, and there was the click of the car's turn signal in the background. "Listen, I'm not going into the parking lot. It's driven by a vampire. The parking fee is $4 an hour. Where are you now?"
Fortunately, Li Wei has been exposed to English since he was a child, which is equivalent to half a native language, otherwise he would not be able to understand the words of this uncle named Don Quixote Cervantes.
Did he actually make some money? Levi couldn't help but wonder, why else would he be so anxious about the $4-an-hour parking fee.
"I'm Levi," he said. "I just went through customs."
"Then go to Terminal 4, Area B, outside Gate 2, and call me when you arrive in 5 minutes," Don Quixote's voice was very urgent, "Don't call too early, do you understand? I can't stop for too long, the damn traffic police are watching me."
After hanging up the phone, Levi stood there a little sluggishly, thinking about whether to use Huabei to pay for another ticket to go back.
Ten minutes later, a dilapidated car with mud spots on its side skirts stopped in the driveway and almost hit a yellow taxi.
It took Levi a while to identify the Toyota, which was originally white, through the thick mortar and rust. The car window rolled down, revealing a thin face with prominent cheekbones and a stubble, with bags under his eyes caused by long-term lack of sleep.
"Get in the car!" His eyes flickered, as if looking for the non-existent traffic police, "Hurry up, don't waste time."
With some difficulty, Levi threw the two heavy boxes into the rear compartment that was filled with dust and empty paint buckets, opened the passenger door and got in.
There was also a reflective vest full of paint spots and a half-empty Gatorade bottle thrown on the passenger seat. Levi threw them into the back seat with some disgust before sitting down.
"Woo!"
Don Quixote stepped on the accelerator, and the Toyota screamed. It did not charge like a knight's horse, but slowly and tremblingly squeezed into the traffic.
"Fasten your seat belt," he turned around and said, "The passenger door latch is broken and it might pop open when you turn a corner."
Levi couldn't help but raise a hand and grab the handle above his head.
"Levi, right?" Don Quixote said, "Listen, I'm sorry for the death of your father... my half-brother and sister-in-law... I'm sorry, he was a really smart guy, but he died in a ridiculous car accident... I heard you lost a lot of money? Can't you afford to come to the United States?"
"I will make money and pay back the money I owe, and it's none of your business," Levi frownedBrows said, "This is my own business. When I grow up, I will go work and make money."
Is this the uncle who "made some money" as his father said before he was alive?
"But when he threw you to me, he didn't bring a check for one million US dollars," Don Quixote sneered. "New York is not as good as China. Money here can buy everything, but it also means that everything must be bought with money. So, how much money do you have in your pocket?"
"About... there is 600 US dollars in the card," Levi said, "The rest is my clothes and some daily necessities."
In fact, he had 2 cards, and the other one contained a full 6,000 US dollars, but he didn't say anything.
This money is used to pay off debts, but for him now it is undoubtedly a huge amount of money that can save his life at a critical moment.
But even 600 US dollars seemed a bit surprising in front of this uncle.
"Six hundred dollars? Ha!" He slapped the steering wheel. "Well, at least it's enough to pay for this week's gas bill and my lost work pay. Welcome to America, kid."
During the chattering along the way, Li Wei did not need to say anything, and Don Quixote naturally told his story like beans from a bamboo tube.
From when he made a small fortune in business, to when he met his ex-wife ("She was a pure bitch, wasn't she? Women are like that, they want to squeeze all your marrow out"), then they got divorced, and there was a problem with the capital chain, so he went to borrow money from the gang. While taking out a loan shark, he also had to pay his ex-wife $2,000 a month in alimony (“Damn American law, you can still earn $2,000 a month by letting a pig lie at home. If I had been 10 years earlier, I would have wanted to sell my butt to make money.”).
"So now I have to work two jobs to survive," he lit up a cigarette and concluded lightly, "I carry bricks at a construction site during the day, and wash dishes in the back kitchen of a Spanish restaurant at night. This is America. If you want to survive, you have to do your best...here we are."
"Where is this?" Levi looked through the greasy car window at the gray concrete building that looked like a moldy loaf of bread.
This certainly doesn't look like Don Quixote's home.
